title: The Corbie Riders' Tally
author: the riders of Corbie Stack
body:
# The riders' tally

*Split birch, notched, with words cut small beside the notches.*

---

**Low Rudd dale.** Seven farms. Six paid. Hobb's did not. Went down at the dark of the moon. Took the heifers, left the house. Annet says the house stands. The house stands.

**The Bone Ford.** The carters pay at the ford by the load. Two loads short. A word with the carter.

**Kharrow Foot.** Nothing. The Moot's wardens on the market. Leave it.

**The Bucket-Line.** The Brindle woman will not pay for the cable. Cut it. *(Under it, in another hand:)* She mended it in a month. Leave her be, Annet says. A woman who mends a thing in a month will mend it again.

**Isbel ko-Rudd's.** Twelve years paid. Twelve. Never late. Annet says send her a ham this midwinter, and nobody is to go near the place.

*(The last notch is new, and cut deep.)*

**Isbel ko-Rudd's.** Her man came up the pass after a heifer that was never ours. Dannan met him. Annet does not know yet.

title: A Bone-Warden's Last Count
author: Orrin ko-Skarl, bone-warden of the Moot
body:
# The last count

*A bone-warden's tally-book, the last pages, swollen with damp.*

---

**Thaw.** The Wading Giant's left shin gone from the beck. Drag-marks up the Upper Dales. Not men: men would have used a sledge.

**Thaw, later.** The Jawbone's lower teeth, three of them. The Brakh's knuckle off the Drink's lip. All the same way, uphill.

**Midsummer.** Found them. They are standing up. I have counted from the scree, with the glass. Forty-one bones that I know by name, and stones between them bound with cord, and the hags going up and down it on ladders like masons on a church. I have written to the Moot. The Moot has written back to ask which clan's land it is on, for the blood-price.

**Midsummer, later.** One of them saw me. She did not throw. She waved me nearer, the way you would a dog.

**Lammas.** I have come down into the warren to count what they keep below. There is a hall at the bottom with every bone heaped in it that the thralls ever carried, and one hag knotting a cord in the middle of them, and she is singing the bones' names. She knows more of them than I do.

*(The rest of the page is a list of bones, very neatly written, and it stops in the middle of a word.)*

title: Swarms in the Top Row
author: Bannoch, bee-master
body:
# The top row

---

**Kharrow's spare swarm, 1009.** Put in the third bole of the top row at dusk. Gone at dawn. Found it in the Kharrow row, in with its sisters, as if it had never left.

**Skarl's, 1012.** Same. Back to the Skarl row by morning.

**A wild swarm off the Rudd road, 1015.** Nobody's bees. Put it in the top row thinking it would have no row to go back to. It went over the crag and into the Answering Wall's rocks, and the callers said for a month the wall hummed.

**1021.** Tried nothing. Swept the boles. Somebody has left a bone token in the fourth. I've left it.

I think the bees go where they are said. Every clan says its own row. Nobody says the top one.

title: Turns in the Wheel
author: Grett ko-Brindle, line-mistress
body:
# Turns walked

*Cut into a board with a knife, a notch a turn, words beside.*

---

**Spring.** Line cut by the Stack's riders. Buckets in the beck. No turns this month. Splicing.

**Summer.** Haddo's boy, forty turns. Cheap. Eats like a horse.

**Summer.** A Ghaleld hewer, twelve turns, to show he could. Could not walk home after.

**Autumn.** Thralls on the far trestle at night, two of them, carrying a giant's shin up the dale towards the Dales. They walked under the line and the buckets swung. Did not stop. Did not look up.

**Autumn.** The rent-rider again. Told him the cable pays no rent and he said Annet says leave her be. Leave me be, then.

title: Lines over the West Moor
author: Runa ko-Oskel
body:
# What the line said

---

**Dawn, west wind.** High and steady. Nothing.

**Noon.** A kick in the line from the north-east, the crows up over the Stack. Flew her low a quarter-hour. Nothing came. Up again.

**Night.** Black kite, lantern. The thing on the Upper Dales is taller. Lights going up it and coming down. Told Haskel when he came by. He wrote it down and went to look.

**Night.** Lantern caught a thrall on the Ghast road carrying a jaw on its back. Big jaw. Not a clan beast's. Going east.

**Night.** Haskel has not come back down. His fire's up there, by the thing. He waves his lantern at mine.

title: Links Closed This Year
author: Ottar ko-Ghast, chain-smith
body:
# This year's links

---

Brenna, Ossi, Tam, Hild. A pair for the Tolly twins, one link, two names. One for Edda's girl with a line under, she did not see the morning.

A bar off a Vale tinker, his own name, said slow. He cried. They mostly do.

A Kharrow bone-carver, for a bet. Paid me in a carved link. Hung it with the rest.

---

*(At the foot of the page, smaller:)* Twelve from the top, the gap. Eleven years. I've a link half-forged for it in the hearth's ash-pit, blank. I don't know what name to put on it, or whether to put one.
